# Embers of the Hollow Sun: the rulebook

The one list of rules in force for the whole project (issue 492, FINDINGS R190). Each rule says what to do, why (the problem
Ryan was reacting to, in his words where they exist), who set it and when, and its old ids. Rules of play and balance numbers
are not here (R190's scope): they live in the browser oracle, godot/rules and their FINDINGS rows (for example battles growing
over a run toward about 20 ships, a guide and not a cap, R1; capture as add, strip or ransom, R4).

Ryan, Nov 11 2026: "Those old hard coded rules with no context or detail artifically restricing us are exactly what I'm worried
about across the board" (R190), and at 20:05 CST: "Let's ensure we're documenting all these decisions and approaches. I don't
want this drift to keep happening or where we get confused on how we're doing things."

Set by: **Ryan** (his own call, his words exist), **Board** (a Claude Board thread wrote it), **agent** (Muse, Codex or a
worker). Ids are FINDINGS rows (R, D, F, G, X) or register ids from contrib/opus/reviews/rules_sweep/.

## 0. How rules work here

0.1 **Every rule carries its reason, beside it.** Why: three old rules with no reason were built to the letter on Nov 11 (sliced
wrecks R186, the flash counter R187, the movement call R189). Ryan: "I think some of the findings got misinterpreted." Set:
Ryan, Nov 11 (R189, R190). A rule nobody can give a reason for does not go in this book.

0.2 **A ruling is landed only when the same pull request edits this book or the working document for its area** (the
playbook, RECIPE.md, AGENTS.md). Why: rulings filed in FINDINGS never reached the documents builders read (R209, R211). Set:
Ryan, Nov 11 (R214). FINDINGS stays as the dated history; this book is the live source. Each FINDINGS row from R281 on
says where it landed ("landed in <repo path>") or says "one-off job decision"; the memory lint
(contrib/opus/tools/memory_lint_tests.js) fails a row that says neither, so a ruling cannot sit in FINDINGS alone (R291,
issue 890).

0.3 **Which document wins.** This book; then the playbook for the area; then AGENTS.md; then briefs. HANDOFF.md and LOOP.md
win for current status only. Between two of Ryan's rulings the later one wins, and the entry here is edited, never only a new
FINDINGS row. Why: corrections written as new rows left the old wording reading as the rule (R183's withdrawn gate line).
Set: Board, Nov 11, from Muse's outside sweep (contrib/muse/reviews/rules_sweep_2026_11.md, Parts 4 and 6).

0.4 **A number in a document is a starting point judged by eye, unless it protects comfort, frame rate, saves, crashes or rules
parity.** A number names its measurement, or says it is a tuning value. Why: every hit size was tuned under a cap that was
never the guideline it cited (R187); Ryan wanted the audit to find "these weird arbitrary, like, guidance on that is making
it, you know, more restricted and less realistic and cinematic than it should be". Set: Ryan, Nov 7 (R121: assumed gates stop
binding until a measurement earns them back) and Nov 11 (R187: "Keep comfort, loosen rest").

0.5 **Order follows the faction; motion and breaks never feel staged.** Hullbreaker armour is irregular patchwork. Eclipse
panels are precise, dead even, ordered and aligned, with seams and slight relief (Ryan, Nov 13, R243: "make the eclipse panels
actually panels and dead even and ordered to align"). Glasswrights are blown glass without panels; Chorus surfaces are grown,
without plates. Sunward and Hegemony follow factions.md. Instant motion, identical beats, straight cuts and one scale still
read as staged. Why: the wrecks "feel like they're just getting sliced in half" (R186); applying that to every faction's
surface erased the Eclipse's machine precision. Set: Ryan's complaints, Board's wording (R187), corrected by Ryan (R243).

0.6 **A rule that rests on a fact that can change names what ends it** (a model's version, a plan's limit, a tool that is
down). Why: the Codex cloud ban, the Fable helper counts and the Kimi sentence outlived their facts. Set: Board, Nov 11 (Muse
sweep Part 4).

0.7 **A rule that says the game does something needs a capture or a check that shows it, or the words "not built yet".** Why:
specs described braking jets and slow motion the game did not have (issue 492). Set: Board, Nov 11.

0.8 **After a day with many rulings, the Board has an outside model check that each one landed in the document a worker reads
(a dropped-context sweep).** Batch rulings that only set a rule (no working method) may land in this book alone. Why: the
insides rule was recorded but never reached the builder's playbook (R209, R211); Muse's method audit found
the screens half of R218 written nowhere (issue 558). Set: Board, Nov 12 (R211, issue 558).

0.9 **How a route is set up (any multi-step pipeline: ships, effects, captures, installs).** (a) A method change is done
only when one real item has gone end to end through it into the game on Ryan's PC; each stage passing alone is not a pass.
(b) Each fact has one home: the first step that decides it writes it, and every later step reads it from there instead of
keeping its own copy; a mirror refreshed from that home under a check (the oracle copies, 12.4) is not a second home. (c) A check tests what its rule says and reads the item's own numbers (length, seams, part shapes),
never the shape of the first item it was written for. (d) Anything Ryan's PC runs (.bat launchers, installs, caches) gets
one real run there before it counts as done, within 3.3 (nothing deleted on the PC without Ryan's yes). No new test or gate is added for this rule; it shapes how routes are built
and briefed. Why: Codex's A16 dry run (issue 587) found eight gaps from these four habits: the build sheet and the recipe
kept separate copies of the same facts, three checks assumed the old C15s cruiser (its 14.5 length, an extra seam,
closed engine bells), a launcher quoting bug and a stale game cache only show on Windows in a real install, and no ship
had gone from sheet to game since the sheet method changed. Set: Board, Nov 12, on Ryan's ask to learn from the gaps at
the level of design and setup, not patches (R225).


0.10 **How the repo carries memory (R251).** A standing rule comes only from Ryan's words, quoted in FINDINGS and landed here; a row
that stretches his words past what he named says so and asks him. Board choices for one day or one job (effort, caps, job order,
wrappers, which seat took a job) are operating notes in LOOP.md, never rules. A new ruling names what it replaces and the old row is
marked SUPERSEDED, so no two live rules conflict. One live place per kind: rules in this book, what is open and who has it on GitHub itself
(checked live before any dispatch; contrib/opus/OPEN_WORK.md is only a timestamped nightly index of it, issue 890), what runs on the PC in LOOP.md's newest LATEST lines and The seats, the hand-over in HANDOFF section 0 (about one page; older sections go to docs/archive), history in FINDINGS.
LOOP.md's LATEST lines roll into a dated summary once they pass about 15. Muse audits for stale or conflicting docs now and then.
Why: several models and fresh chats read the repo cold; on Nov 14 a one-day choice nearly became a rule, an A20 note was stretched to
every ship before Ryan ratified it (R244), and a summary line inverted Ryan's call on A18 and A19.

# The Fable program: one finished battle, and playbooks other models can run

Issue 405. FINDINGS R167. Written by the Board (Fable 5.2), Nov 10 2026.

## What Ryan asked for

"I still have another full fable reset, so we can use fable on the really key stuff. Design, graphics, effects, etc. let's do
everything we can to use the fable resets smart here. Playbooks or recipes, deep reviews and redesign, etc. codebase is yours
with my direction and vision, you bring it to life with the decisions needed from me. I want this to end with something that
opus or other models can run from" (Nov 10 2026, 08:42 CST).

His scope answers:
- Focus, in this order of weight: battle effects, ships, space and the board. Screens and sound still get a playbook, lighter.
- End state: "One finished battle + playbooks".
- Steering: "Options first, then build". He sees two or three options, picks one, then it is built.
- Decisions: "As they come". Two lines and one image, whenever a pick is ready.

## The end state

1. **One finished battle.** A single fight that looks and reads final from the first shot to the last wreck, at the camera the
   game is really played at (camera 170 on the look bench). It is the proof that the recipes work and the reference every
   later job is judged against.
2. **A playbook per area**, written from what that battle needed, so another model can do the next ship, effect, hex or
   screen without asking: docs/playbooks/effects.md, ships.md, space.md, screens.md, sound.md.
3. **The front door**: HANDOFF.md section 0 and AGENTS.md point at the playbooks, and the job board holds the remaining items
   as ready jobs written from each playbook's job template.

## The finished battle (what "final" means here)

- **Board**: the dead-star gravity-well board (owner ruling, Oct 24).
- **Fleets**: about six to eight ships a side. **Sunward Crusade against Eclipse** (Ryan, Nov 11 2026, R180; this replaces the
  first plan of the Hullbreakers plus one other). Both have a settled flagship (docs/playbooks/factions.md) and look nothing
  alike. Each fleet needs one capital, one cruiser or destroyer and one escort through the ship recipe.
- **Ships**: built by tools/recipe with real thickness and comprehensive insides (R98, R209, R215), hard points by hull class
  and faction theme (R164 item 4, issue 363), from an accepted concept in the one style (R197) and an Opus build sheet that
  passes the concept standard (R203, R205, R207; docs/playbooks/ships.md).
- **Effects**: every big moment staged to Muse's table (contrib/muse/design/hit_staging_2026_11/synthesis.md): explosions by
  the picked route (issues 353, 365), deaths in three beats (366), one kit of trails, beams and flares (367), effects that
  start on the ship (370), shields that hug the hull with one shield pool, per-side coverage and lossy power routing, resting as Rim and Gap (R246 replaces R163 item 2's four strengths and invisible rest; 371 rules first, then 372 the look; design in contrib/muse/design/shields_2026_11/).
- **Space**: nebula and ion storm hexes with depth (368), a board planet and rocks from real data, remixed past recognition
  (R163 item 3; 369), the black hole and sky calm enough that ships and effects win.
- **Screen**: the battle screen in the ember orders-sheet look, layout E1 Ledger, shield readouts in Glacier #92b8e8 (Ryan,
  Nov 11: "Retire lime", R191; "E1 Ledger" and "Glacier pale blue", R210). Being built: issue 271 step 2.
- **Sound**: scoped (R171: weapons, hits and deaths, buttons and menus, ambience, music; "Clean and tactical"). Routing is in
  (issue 506); sound weight is next (R193 (4)); the redo follows the listening page.
- **Done**: a capture of the whole fight and its look bench sheet, and Ryan says yes.

## How every item flows

1. **Options.** Fable makes two or three options: a bench sheet of real captures where the thing exists, a flat mockup where
   it does not. Cheap, fast, and never more than one sheet per decision.
2. **Pick.** Ryan picks, with one image and two lines in front of him. The pick is recorded in FINDINGS with his words.
3. **Build.** The seat the table below names builds it. One worked example first, never the whole set.
4. **Proof.** The look bench before and after, at camera 170 first (bench a commit twice, keep the second run), plus the
   area's own check. Fable looks at the pictures, not the claim.
5. **Recipe.** What worked is written into the area's playbook the same day: target, steps, check, traps, job template.
6. **Roll out.** The rest of that kind (the other 34 hulls, the other weapons, the other hexes) becomes jobs written from the
   playbook's template, for DeepSeek, Codex or Opus. Fable only reviews their pictures.

Standing rules for every flow (Nov 16 2026, issue 880): the run brief lives in the issue body, one current instruction
(R281); an open issue is not proof of undone work, and a merge closes its issue in the same step when its scope is done
(R288); every picture carries its revision and stage; and visual work is compared with its concept and ruling, with the
misses stated plainly, before it merges (RULEBOOK 2.3 and 2.4).

## How a run works

1. Read HANDOFF.md section 0 and this file. Set the lock and push it first.
2. Board check: open PRs, open issues and labels (gh api REST, never GraphQL). PC queue folders only when a PC job is running.
3. Review each new PR yourself, by diff, never by title, then sweep its impact (R129): every caller of each changed function, save and old-profile behaviour, the JS and Godot twins, every UI path that shows it, which tests actually ran in CI. Check claims against the done-when, look at the shots. Read the PR's Artoo comments on its current head commit and settle each (verify against live main; evidence, not rulings; R295). Merge if good; hold what Holds lists; file a follow-up for anything the sweep finds. Outside-check conditions still open at merge become issues (the PR 680 form) or a line in the PR's FINDINGS row, so none rides on memory (Muse audit 706 finding 10).
4. Release the next job only to a live seat, one at a time. Before releasing, check it is not already queued or running.
5. Anything for Ryan goes under "Waiting on Ryan" with a pick and plain trade-offs. In an unattended run use one PushNotification, never AskUserQuestion.
6. Tell Ryan only when something lands or needs him: two lines and one image.
7. Rewrite this file, set "Running: no", commit straight to main (this file and FINDINGS only, docs-only exception), push with timeout 90. Stop.
8. One send_later check only when a job or a limit reset lands well before the next look. Never chain them.

"""Stage 7 install and the standalone ship manifest merge used by the look bench."""
import contextlib
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile


HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ENTRY = 'manifest_entry.json'


@contextlib.contextmanager
def project_lock(project):
    # The OS releases the lock even if the installer exits. Keep the lock file so
    # later installers always lock the same file.
    with (project / '.stage7.lock').open('a+b') as lock:
        try:
            if os.name == 'nt':
                import msvcrt
                lock.seek(0)
                msvcrt.locking(lock.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
            else:
                import fcntl
                fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(f'another ship install is using {project}') from exc
        yield


def sha256(path):
    with path.open('rb') as source:
        return hashlib.file_digest(source, 'sha256').hexdigest()


def verify(folder, expected):
    for name, digest in expected.items():
        if sha256(folder / name) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f'{folder / name} differs from the checked export')


def copy_verified(source, dest, digest=None):
    expected = sha256(source) if digest is None else digest
    shutil.copy2(source, dest)
    if sha256(dest) != expected:
        raise ValueError(f'copy verification failed for {dest}')


def backup_file(source, dest):
    if source.exists():
        copy_verified(source, dest)
        return dest
    return None


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_bytes())


def merge_entry(entry, previous, code, dest):
    manifest = read_json(previous) if previous else dict(note='', ships={})
    manifest.setdefault('ships', {})[code] = entry
    dest.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=1), encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')


def main(entry_path, godot, code):
    """Keep the existing manifest-only command for the look-bench overlay."""
    project = Path(godot).resolve()
    with project_lock(project):
        path = project / 'assets' / 'ships' / 'manifest.json'
        work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='manifest.bak_', dir=path.parent))
        previous = backup_file(path, work / path.name)
        entry = read_json(Path(entry_path))
        new = work / 'new.json'
        merge_entry(entry, previous, code, new)
        os.replace(new, path)
    print(f'manifest PASS: {code} written into {path} with points {entry.get("hardpoints", {})}')
    return 0


def export_snapshot(export, snapshot, code):
    # The GLB names the texture set. A previous export can leave other JPGs
    # in the same directory, so the install must never use a wildcard copy.
    from check_export import read_glb

    glb = code + '.glb'
    copy_verified(export / glb, snapshot / glb)
    doc, _ = read_glb(snapshot / glb)
    maps = {image.get('uri') for image in doc.get('images', [])}
    for name in maps:
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not re.fullmatch(re.escape(code) + r'_[\w-]+\.jpg', name):
            raise ValueError(f'unsupported export texture path {name!r}')
    for name in [ENTRY, *sorted(maps)]:
        copy_verified(export / name, snapshot / name)
    return {name: sha256(snapshot / name) for name in [glb, ENTRY, *sorted(maps)]}


def run_check(command, log, marker=None):
    with log.open('w', encoding='utf-8') as output:
        result = subprocess.run(command, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    report = log.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if marker is None or result.returncode or marker not in report:
        print(report, end='')
    if result.returncode or (marker is not None and marker not in report):
        raise RuntimeError(f'check failed. See {log}')


def install(project, code, snapshot, expected, refresh, readback):
    """Publish the checked files and roll the ship and its cache back together."""
    ship_base = project / 'assets' / 'ships'
    live = ship_base / code
    manifest = ship_base / 'manifest.json'
    gen_manifest = project / 'gen' / 'manifest.json'
    scene = project / 'gen' / 'ships' / (code + '.scn')
    files = {name: digest for name, digest in expected.items() if name != ENTRY}

    with project_lock(project):
        verify(snapshot, expected)
        ship_base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='.stage7-replaced-', dir=project))
        incoming = work / 'incoming' / code
        incoming.mkdir(parents=True)
        replaced = work / 'previous'
        replaced.mkdir()
        failed = work / 'failed'
        failed.mkdir()

        def managed(name):
            return (name in files or name in {code + '_damage.glb', code + '_wreck.glb'}
                    or (name.startswith(code + '_') and name.lower().endswith('.jpg')))

        # Keep other files in the ship directory, and stage every copy and
        # manifest backup before the first live change.
        if live.exists():
            shutil.copytree(live, incoming, dirs_exist_ok=True,
                            ignore=lambda directory, names: [name for name in names if managed(name)]
                            if Path(directory) == live else [])
        for name, digest in files.items():
            copy_verified(snapshot / name, incoming / name, digest)
        previous_manifest = backup_file(manifest, replaced / 'asset_manifest.json')
        previous_cache = backup_file(gen_manifest, replaced / 'cache_manifest.json')
        entry = read_json(snapshot / ENTRY)
        verify(snapshot, expected)
        new_manifest = work / 'manifest.json'
        merge_entry(entry, previous_manifest, code, new_manifest)
        manifest_digest = sha256(new_manifest)

        def verify_install():
            verify(live, files)
            if sha256(manifest) != manifest_digest:
                raise ValueError('installed ship manifest differs from the checked export')
            if any(managed(path.name) and path.name not in files for path in live.iterdir()):
                raise ValueError('obsolete export files remain in the ship folder')

        changes = []
        try:
            previous_ship = replaced / code if live.exists() else None
            if previous_ship:
                os.replace(live, previous_ship)
            changes.append((live, previous_ship, code))

            previous_scene = replaced / 'ship.scn' if scene.exists() else None
            if previous_scene:
                os.replace(scene, previous_scene)
            changes.append((scene, previous_scene, 'ship.scn'))
            changes.append((gen_manifest, previous_cache, 'cache_manifest.json'))
            # Only this ship is visible to the builder. Moving the old scene
            # aside forces a rebuild even when old and new stamps collide.
            refresh(incoming.parent)

            os.replace(incoming, live)

            os.replace(new_manifest, manifest)
            changes.append((manifest, previous_manifest, 'asset_manifest.json'))
            verify_install()
            readback()
            verify_install()
        except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt):
            errors = []
            for dest, previous, name in reversed(changes):
                try:
                    if previous is not None and previous.is_file():
                        os.replace(previous, dest)
                    else:
                        if dest.exists():
                            os.replace(dest, failed / name)
                        if previous is not None:
                            os.replace(previous, dest)
                except OSError as exc:
                    errors.append(str(exc))
            if errors:
                raise RuntimeError(f'rollback incomplete. Backups at {work}: ' + ' | '.join(errors)) from None
            print(f'Install rolled back. Recovery files at {work}', file=sys.stderr)
            raise
        print(f'Installed into {live}; previous files at {replaced}')


def install_export(export, project, code, godot, job, ship, *options):
    export, project, job, ship = (Path(path).resolve() for path in (export, project, job, ship))
    if not (project / 'project.godot').is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'INSTALL_TO is not a Godot project folder: {project}')
    if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*', code):
        raise ValueError(f'invalid ship folder code {code!r}')

    snapshot = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f'stage7-checked-{code}-'))
    expected = export_snapshot(export, snapshot, code)
    for script, log, failed in (
        ('check_export.py', 'log_export_check.txt', 'CHECK FAILED'),
        ('check_export_selftest.py', 'log_export_selftest.txt', 'SELFTEST FAILED'),
    ):
        try:
            run_check([sys.executable, '-B', str(HERE / script), str(ship), str(snapshot), *options], job / log)
        except RuntimeError:
            (export / 'export_status.txt').write_text(failed + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
            raise
    verify(snapshot, expected)
    copy_verified(snapshot / (code + '_check.json'), export / (code + '_check.json'))
    with (export / 'export_status.txt').open('a', encoding='utf-8') as status:
        status.write('CHECKED\n')

    def headless(script, args, log, marker):
        run_check([godot, '--headless', '--path', str(project), '--script', script, '--', *args], job / log, marker)

    def refresh(ships):
        headless('res://render/build_assets.gd', ['--ships-only', '--ships', ships.as_posix()],
                 'log_install_cache.txt', '[assets] ships refreshed:')

    def readback():
        headless('res://render/test/installed_ship_check.gd', [code],
                 'log_install_readback.txt', f'INSTALL READBACK PASS code={code} ')
        for line in (job / 'log_install_readback.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').splitlines():
            if line.startswith('INSTALL READBACK PASS'):
                print(line)

    install(project, code, snapshot, expected, refresh, readback)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        args = sys.argv[1:]
        if len(args) >= 7 and args[0] == '--install':
            sys.exit(install_export(*args[1:]))
        if len(args) == 3:
            sys.exit(main(*args))
        sys.exit('usage: manifest_merge.py ENTRY PROJECT CODE or --install EXPORT PROJECT CODE GODOT JOB SHIP_JSON [unbaked=1]')
    except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        sys.exit(f'Stage 7 FAILED: {exc}')

def join(objs, name):
    """join copies into one object named name (world space, no parent)"""
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for c in objs: c.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = objs[0]; bpy.ops.object.join(); j = bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active
    if j.parent is not None:
        mw = j.matrix_world.copy(); j.parent = None; j.matrix_world = mw
    j.name = name; j.data.name = name; bpy.ops.object.material_slot_remove_unused()
    for k in list(j.keys()): del j[k]
    return j

keep = [prep(o) for o in src if o.name not in TURNING]      # the ship mesh: everything but the turning parts of turrets
J = join(keep, CODE)
TURN_OBJS = [join([prep(o) for o in ms], f'turret_{k}_turn') for k, (pv, ms) in enumerate(PIVOTS)]
used_materials = {slot.material.name for o in [J] + TURN_OBJS for slot in o.material_slots if slot.material}
destruction['interior_materials'] = [m for m in destruction['interior_materials'] if m in used_materials]
J.data.calc_loop_triangles(); TRIS = len(J.data.loop_triangles)
TURRET_TRIS = 0
for t in TURN_OBJS:
    t.data.calc_loop_triangles(); TURRET_TRIS += len(t.data.loop_triangles)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- materials and maps
def occlusion_group():
    ng = bpy.data.node_groups.get('glTF Material Output')
    if ng is None:
        ng = bpy.data.node_groups.new('glTF Material Output', 'ShaderNodeTree')
        ng.interface.new_socket('Occlusion', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketFloat')
    return ng

def resize_atlas(image, role):
    image.scale(MAPS, MAPS)
    # Scaling a packed Blender image does not mark it dirty. Set the pixels so
    # the glTF exporter encodes the resized buffer from memory.
    pixels = np.empty(MAPS * MAPS * 4, dtype=np.float32)
    image.pixels.foreach_get(pixels)
    if role == 'normal':
        vectors = pixels.reshape(-1, 4)[:, :3]
        vectors *= 2.0
        vectors -= 1.0
        lengths = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        valid = lengths[:, 0] > 1e-6
        np.divide(vectors, lengths, out=vectors, where=valid[:, None])
        vectors[~valid] = (0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        vectors += 1.0
        vectors *= 0.5
    image.pixels.foreach_set(pixels)
    image.update()


if UNBAKED:      # test only: the plain role materials set before the join (<CODE>_hull, <CODE>_parts) so the glb still loads; no maps
    for s in J.material_slots: s.material.use_nodes = True

def empty(name, p, fwd, up, extras):
    """an empty whose glTF node has -Z along fwd and +Y along up. The exporter turns Blender's axes (x, y, z) into glTF's
    (x, z, -y) for positions and rotations alike, so in Blender the empty's +Y is fwd and its +Z is up."""
    f = Vector(fwd).normalized(); u = Vector(up).normalized()
    if abs(u.dot(f)) > .85: u = Vector((0, 0, 1))      # a gun aimed straight out of its mount: 'away from the hull' is the barrel itself, so up is up
    u = (u - f * u.dot(f))
    if u.length < 1e-4: u = Vector((0, 0, 1)) - f * f.z
    if u.length < 1e-4: u = Vector((0, 1, 0))
    u.normalize(); x = f.cross(u).normalized()
    o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, None); sc.collection.objects.link(o); o.empty_display_size = .01
    R = Matrix((x, f, u)).transposed().to_4x4(); R.translation = Vector(p); o.matrix_world = R; o.parent = J; o.matrix_parent_inverse = Matrix.Identity(4)
    o.matrix_world = R
    for k, v in extras.items(): o[k] = v
    return o

"""Check the A16 seam fixture, or rebuild the fixture and its record together.

   python tools/recipe/sheet_fixture_hash.py --check
   python tools/recipe/sheet_fixture_hash.py --bake BLENDER_EXE
   python tools/recipe/sheet_fixture_hash.py --bake BLENDER_EXE --out DIR

--out DIR bakes a fresh pair into DIR and leaves the committed fixture alone (issue 1174: CI bakes into its temp folder when
the record is stale, then runs death_seam_check.gd on DIR/C19_51_unbaked.glb.gz). --check --quiet-stale exits 3, not 1,
when the record is only stale, so CI can tell "rebake" from a broken record.

The first record line, file list and data.js extract also feed death_seam_check.gd.
The last line pins the exact gzip bytes used by the CI fixture check.
"""
import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
HULL_BUILDER = 'tools/blender/r209/sheet_hull.py'
EXPORTER = 'tools/recipe/export7.py'
SHIP_JSON = 'tools/recipe/ships/corsair_A16.json'
FILES = (
    'tools/blender/build_sheets/ships/corsair_A16.py',
    'tools/blender/build_sheets/kit.py',
    'tools/blender/kits/hullbreakers/parts.py',
    'tools/blender/build_sheets/contract.py',
    'tools/blender/build_sheets/variants.py',
    EXPORTER, HULL_BUILDER, SHIP_JSON,
    'tools/blender/kits/shared/hardpoints.py',
    'tools/blender/kits/shared/turrets.py',
    'tools/recipe/gamedata.py',
)
OUT = REPO / 'godot/fx/test/fixtures/C19_51_unbaked.sheet.txt'
FIXTURE = OUT.with_name('C19_51_unbaked.glb.gz')
EXTRACT_MARK = '# data.js entry %s: the fields the build reads (tools/recipe/gamedata.py), sorted keys, JSON'


def extract():
    """Hash the A16 fields used by the build, so unrelated rules edits do not mark it stale."""
    import gamedata
    with (REPO / SHIP_JSON).open(encoding='utf-8') as source:
        ship = json.load(source)
    game = ship['game_ship']
    fields = dict(cls=gamedata.ship_attr(game, 'cls', default='Cruiser'),
                  fac=gamedata.ship_attr(game, 'fac', default=ship.get('faction')),
                  hangar=int(gamedata.ship_attr(game, 'hangar', default=0) or 0),
                  weapons=[list(w) for w in gamedata.weapons(game)])
    return json.dumps(fields, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), game


def digest(text):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in FILES:
        h.update((REPO / name).read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n'))
    h.update((text + '\n').encode('utf-8'))
    return h.hexdigest()


def record(text, game, input_digest, fixture_bytes):
    fixture_digest = hashlib.sha256(fixture_bytes).hexdigest()
    return '\n'.join((f'sha256 {input_digest}', *FILES, EXTRACT_MARK % game, text,
                      f'# fixture sha256 {fixture_digest}', ''))


class Stale(ValueError):
    """The record no longer matches the A16 inputs or the compressed GLB: a rebake fixes it."""


def check(out=None, fixture=None):
    out, fixture = out or OUT, fixture or FIXTURE
    text, game = extract()
    expected = record(text, game, digest(text), fixture.read_bytes())
    if out.read_text(encoding='utf-8') != expected:
        raise Stale('fixture record is stale or the compressed GLB changed. Rebuild with --bake.')
    print('PASS fixture record matches the A16 inputs and compressed GLB')


def bake(blender, dest=None):
    text, game = extract()
    input_digest = digest(text)
    ship_path = REPO / SHIP_JSON
    ship = json.loads(ship_path.read_bytes())
    work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='a16-fixture-'))
    export = work / 'export'
    env = dict(os.environ, R209_SHIP=str(ship_path))

    def run_blender(*args):
        command = [blender, *map(str, args)]
        if os.name == 'nt':
            watchdog = REPO / 'tools/pc/tmo.bat'
            command = [str(watchdog), '21600', *command]
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, env=env, check=True)

    run_blender('-b', '--python-exit-code', '1', '-P', REPO / HULL_BUILDER, '--', work, ship['cell'])
    run_blender('-b', work / (ship['cell'] + '.blend'), '--python-exit-code', '1', '-P', REPO / EXPORTER,
                '--', ship_path, export, 'maps=2048', 'unbaked=1')
    if not (export / 'export_status.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').startswith('WRITTEN '):
        raise ValueError(f'A16 export was not written. See {work}')
    glb = (export / (ship['game_code'] + '.glb')).read_bytes()
    if not glb.startswith(b'glTF'):
        raise ValueError(f'A16 export is not a GLB. See {work}')
    if extract() != (text, game) or digest(text) != input_digest:
        raise ValueError('A16 inputs changed during the bake. Run it again.')
    compressed = gzip.compress(glb, compresslevel=9, mtime=0)
    # Stage both files on the destination volume. An interrupted publish is
    # caught by --check, since the record describes one exact compressed file.
    out, fixture = (OUT, FIXTURE) if dest is None else (Path(dest) / OUT.name, Path(dest) / FIXTURE.name)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=out.parent, delete=False) as output:
        output.write(compressed)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=out.parent, delete=False) as metadata:
        metadata.write(record(text, game, input_digest, compressed).encode('utf-8'))
    os.replace(output.name, fixture)
    os.replace(metadata.name, out)
    check(out, fixture)
    print(f'BAKED {fixture}')


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    mode.add_argument('--check', action='store_true')
    mode.add_argument('--bake', metavar='BLENDER_EXE')
    parser.add_argument('--out', metavar='DIR', help='with --bake: write the fresh pair here, not over the committed one')
    parser.add_argument('--quiet-stale', action='store_true', help='with --check: exit 3 when the record is only stale')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.out and not args.bake:
        parser.error('--out goes with --bake')
    try:
        if args.check:
            check()
        else:
            bake(args.bake, args.out)
    except Stale as exc:
        print('STALE' if args.quiet_stale else 'FAIL', exc)
        return 3 if args.quiet_stale else 1
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc:
        print('FAIL', exc)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

"""Fault checks for stage 7. All writes go to a temporary project."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import tempfile
from unittest.mock import patch

import manifest_merge as stage


CODE = 'TEST_1101'
GLB = CODE + '.glb'
JPG = CODE + '_base.jpg'
OLD_MAP = CODE + '_old.jpg'


def check_snapshot(root):
    export, snapshot = root / 'export', root / 'checked'
    export.mkdir(parents=True)
    snapshot.mkdir()
    doc = json.dumps({'images': [{'uri': JPG}]}).encode('utf-8')
    doc += b' ' * (-len(doc) % 4)
    glb = struct.pack('<4sIII4s', b'glTF', 2, 20 + len(doc), len(doc), b'JSON') + doc
    (export / GLB).write_bytes(glb)
    (export / JPG).write_bytes(b'checked texture')
    (export / OLD_MAP).write_bytes(b'left over from a previous export')
    (export / stage.ENTRY).write_bytes(b'{}')
    expected = stage.export_snapshot(export, snapshot, CODE)
    assert set(expected) == {GLB, JPG, stage.ENTRY}
    assert {path.name for path in snapshot.iterdir()} == set(expected)
    stage.verify(snapshot, expected)
    print('PASS exact export set')


def setup(root):
    snapshot = root / 'checked'
    snapshot.mkdir(parents=True)
    (snapshot / GLB).write_bytes(b'checked hull')
    (snapshot / JPG).write_bytes(b'checked texture')
    (snapshot / stage.ENTRY).write_text('{"hardpoints":{"core":1}}', encoding='utf-8')
    expected = {path.name: stage.sha256(path) for path in snapshot.iterdir()}

    project = root / 'project with spaces'
    live = project / 'assets' / 'ships' / CODE
    scene = project / 'gen' / 'ships' / (CODE + '.scn')
    live.mkdir(parents=True)
    scene.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    originals = {live / GLB: b'old hull', live / JPG: b'old texture',
                 live / OLD_MAP: b'old map', live / (CODE + '_wreck.glb'): b'old wreck',
                 live / (CODE + '_damage.glb'): b'old damage', live / 'notes.txt': b'keep',
                 live.parent / 'manifest.json': b'{"ships":{"other":{"keep":true}}}',
                 scene: b'old cached scene', scene.parent.parent / 'manifest.json': b'old cache manifest'}
    for path, data in originals.items():
        path.write_bytes(data)
    (project / 'project.godot').touch()
    return project, live, scene, snapshot, expected, originals


def exercise(root, fault):
    project, live, scene, snapshot, expected, originals = setup(root)
    manifest = live.parent / 'manifest.json'
    cache = scene.parent.parent / 'manifest.json'
    refreshed = False

    def refresh(ships):
        nonlocal refreshed
        refreshed = True
        assert [child.name for child in ships.iterdir()] == [CODE]
        assert (ships / CODE / GLB).read_bytes() == b'checked hull'
        assert not scene.exists(), 'the old cache scene could suppress a rebuild'
        # A second stage or manifest-only merge cannot write inside this window.
        try:
            stage.main(snapshot / stage.ENTRY, project, 'another_ship')
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            assert 'another ship install' in str(exc)
        else:
            raise AssertionError('a second installer acquired the project lock')
        scene.write_bytes(b'new cached scene')
        cache.write_bytes(b'new cache manifest')
        if fault == 'refresh':
            raise RuntimeError('injected refresh failure')

    def readback():
        assert scene.read_bytes() == b'new cached scene'
        assert (live / GLB).read_bytes() == b'checked hull'
        assert (live / JPG).read_bytes() == b'checked texture'
        assert (live / 'notes.txt').read_bytes() == b'keep'
        assert set(path.name for path in live.iterdir()) == {GLB, JPG, 'notes.txt'}
        assert json.loads(manifest.read_bytes())['ships'] == {
            'other': {'keep': True}, CODE: {'hardpoints': {'core': 1}}}
        if fault == 'readback':
            raise RuntimeError('injected readback failure')
        if fault == 'changed_installed_map':
            (live / JPG).write_bytes(b'wrong installed texture')

    real_copy = stage.shutil.copy2
    real_replace = stage.os.replace
    manifest_publishes = 0

    def copy(source, target, *args, **kwargs):
        if (fault == 'backup_copy' and source == cache) or (fault == 'stage_copy' and source == snapshot / JPG):
            raise PermissionError('injected copy failure')
        return real_copy(source, target, *args, **kwargs)

    def replace(src, dest):
        nonlocal manifest_publishes
        if fault == 'backup_move' and src == scene:
            raise PermissionError('injected backup move failure')
        if dest == manifest and src.name == 'manifest.json':
            manifest_publishes += 1
            assert manifest.read_bytes() == originals[manifest]
        return real_replace(src, dest)

    if fault == 'changed_checked_glb':
        (snapshot / GLB).write_bytes(b'changed checked hull')

    with patch.object(stage.shutil, 'copy2', copy), patch.object(stage.os, 'replace', replace):
        try:
            stage.install(project, CODE, snapshot, expected, refresh, readback)
        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
            assert fault is not None, exc
            assert 'injected' in str(exc) or 'differs from the checked export' in str(exc), exc
        else:
            assert fault is None, f'{fault} was accepted'

    if fault:

    with stage.project_lock(project):
        pass
    print(f'PASS {fault or "install"}')

'use strict';
// R293: shared capacity by load, or one solo measurement. Node 22, no packages.
// All tools copies read ROOT/gpu_slots.json: { "sharedSlots": 2 } (missing = 2).
// The watchdog owns the claim, so killing its tree leaves a reclaimable dead PID.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const net = require('net');
const crypto = require('crypto');
const sleep = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
const slotName = index => 'gpu_slot_' + index;
const realClock = { now: () => performance.now(), sleep };
// The longest admission wait. ship_job.bat defaults to it (issue 1174): on Nov 19 three helpers queued at once and the
// 300 s default failed them. Ship jobs run the helper from their own branch checkout, so raising this only helps once every
// ship branch carries the change.
const MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 3600;
function positiveInteger(value, label) {
  const number = Number(value);
  if (!/^[0-9]+$/.test(String(value)) || !Number.isSafeInteger(number) || number < 1) {
    throw new Error(label + ' must be a positive integer');
  }
  return number;
}
const alive = pid => {
  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return false;
  try { process.kill(pid, 0); return true; } catch (e) { return e.code === 'EPERM'; }
};

// An OS-owned localhost bind serializes short file transactions across ALL tools
// copies. The OS drops it after a crash. No lock or job files are ever deleted.
// No client connects and no data is sent. An occupied port fails closed (waits).
// clock: { now, sleep } (tests pass a fake one, so no test races the wall clock; issue 1174). When the deadline has passed,
// check() runs once more before the lock's own message: an admission that runs out while the lock is busy reports
// "admission timed out", whichever of the two clocks reads first (the Nov 19 CI flake at gpu_slots_tests.js:159).
async function transaction(fn, check = () => {}, deadline, clock = realClock) {
  if (deadline === undefined) deadline = clock.now() + 5000;
  for (;;) {
    check();
    if (clock.now() >= deadline) { check(); throw new Error('GPU slot lock timed out'); }
    const server = net.createServer(socket => socket.destroy());
    const bound = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      server.once('error', e => e.code === 'EADDRINUSE' ? resolve(false) : reject(e));
      server.listen({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 47847, exclusive: true }, () => resolve(true));
    });
    if (!bound) { await clock.sleep(25); continue; }
    try { check(); return fn(); } finally { await new Promise(resolve => server.close(resolve)); }
  }
}

class Slots {
  constructor(root, isAlive = alive) { this.root = root; this.isAlive = isAlive; }
  capacity() {
    const config = this.read('gpu_slots.json');
    // Only a missing file uses the default. A damaged setting fails closed.
    if (config === null && !fs.existsSync(path.join(this.root, 'gpu_slots.json'))) return 2;
    return positiveInteger(config?.sharedSlots, 'gpu_slots.json sharedSlots');
  }
  names() {
    try { return fs.readdirSync(this.root).filter(name => /^gpu_slot_[1-9][0-9]*$/.test(name)).concat('gpu_solo'); }
    catch (e) { if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return ['gpu_solo']; throw e; }
  }
  read(name) {
    try {
      const text = fs.readFileSync(path.join(this.root, name), 'utf8').trim();
      return text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
    } catch (e) {
      if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return null;
      // A damaged holder file must never silently grant another worker a slot.
      throw e;
    }
  }
  write(name, value) {
    fs.mkdirSync(this.root, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(this.root, name), value ? JSON.stringify(value) + '\n' : '');
  }
  cleared() {
    try { return /^GPU cleared(?:\s*:.*)?$/i.test(fs.readFileSync(path.join(this.root, 'gpu_go.txt'), 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/)[0].trim()); }
    catch (e) { if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return false; throw e; }
  }
  checkWeight(holder) {
    const capacity = this.capacity();
    const weight = positiveInteger(holder.weight ?? 1, 'GPU weight');
    if (holder.mode === 'shared' && weight > capacity) throw new Error(`GPU weight ${weight} exceeds shared capacity ${capacity}`);
    return { capacity, weight };
  }
  step(holder, waiterPid = holder.pid) {
    const { capacity, weight } = this.checkWeight(holder);
    const state = this.names().map(name => {
      const item = this.read(name);
      if (item && !this.isAlive(item.pid)) { this.write(name, null); return null; }
      return item;
    });
    if (!this.isAlive(holder.pid)) throw new Error('GPU admission cancelled: owner exited');
    if (!this.cleared()) return null;
    // Include claims above a lowered capacity until they exit or are reclaimed.
    const occupied = state.slice(0, -1).filter(Boolean);
    const pending = state[state.length - 1];
    if (holder.mode === 'solo') {
      if (pending && pending.token !== holder.token) return null;
      // Reserve priority before draining existing shared workers. New workers wait.
      // While draining, the waiting helper owns the reservation. If it is killed
      // outright, the next caller can reclaim it even if the watchdog is alive.
      if (!pending) this.write('gpu_solo', { ...holder, pid: waiterPid });
      if (occupied.length) return null;
      this.write('gpu_slot_1', holder);
      this.write('gpu_solo', holder);
      return holder;
    }
    if (pending || occupied.some(item => item && item.mode === 'solo')) return null;
    if (occupied.length + weight > capacity) return null;
    // One holder occupies every unit of its weight, with admission serialized.
    // Keep the existing file names so claims survive tools updates.
    const free = [];
    for (let index = 1; free.length < weight; index++) {
      const name = slotName(index);
      if (!this.read(name)) free.push(name);
    }
    for (const name of free) this.write(name, holder);
    return holder;
  }
  release(token) {
    for (const name of this.names()) if (this.read(name)?.token === token) this.write(name, null);
  }
}

function weightFor(exe, requested = '', mode = 'shared') {
  if (!mode || mode === 'none') return 0;
  if (requested !== '') return positiveInteger(requested, 'PC_GPU_WEIGHT');
  return /^blender(?:\.exe)?$/i.test(path.win32.basename(exe)) ? 2 : 1;
}

    def __encode_from_image(self, image: bpy.types.Image, export_settings) -> bytes:
        # See if there is an existing file we can use.
        data = None
        # Sequence image can't be exported, but it avoid to crash to check that default image exists
        # Else, it can crash when trying to access a non existing image
        if image.source in ['FILE', 'SEQUENCE'] and not image.is_dirty:
            if image.packed_file is not None:
                data = image.packed_file.data
            else:
                src_path = bpy.path.abspath(image.filepath_raw)
                if os.path.isfile(src_path):
                    with open(src_path, 'rb') as f:
                        data = f.read()
        # Check magic number is right
        if data:
            if self.file_format == 'PNG':
                if data.startswith(b'\x89PNG'):
                    return data
            elif self.file_format == 'JPEG':
                if data.startswith(b'\xff\xd8\xff'):
                    return data
            elif self.file_format == 'WEBP':
                if data[8:12] == b'WEBP':
                    return data

        with TmpImageGuard() as guard:
            make_temp_image_copy(guard, src_image=image)
            tmp_image = guard.image
            return _encode_temp_image(tmp_image, self.file_format, export_settings)

def _encode_temp_image(tmp_image: bpy.types.Image, file_format: str, export_settings) -> bytes:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
        tmpfilename = tmpdirname + '/img'
        tmp_image.filepath_raw = tmpfilename

        tmp_image.file_format = file_format

        try:
            # if image is jpeg, use quality export settings
            if file_format in ["JPEG", "WEBP"]:
                tmp_image.save(quality=export_settings['gltf_image_quality'])
            else:
                tmp_image.save()

            with open(tmpfilename, "rb") as f:
                return f.read()
        except Exception as e:
            export_settings['log'].error("Error while saving image: %s" % e)
            return b''

# Ship recipe, stage 7: the game export, automated (issue 209 round 7; FINDINGS R155, R156: the recipe writes the hard points as a
# required output, and the effects are built to that contract).
# From a ship's baked blend (stage 5) and its ship json, with no hand steps, this writes the game's ship folder
# (godot/assets/ships/README.md, tools/blender/a4/K1_DECISIONS.md):
#   <CODE>.glb             one ship node <CODE> (one mesh; surfaces <CODE>_hull, <CODE>_parts, <CODE>_glow) with an empty child node per
#                          hard point; the maps are outside the glb, by relative URI, as the A4 ships have them. Each turret
#                          (issue 560) is its own child node turret_<n> at its ring centre (+Y the turning axis, -Z the rest aim),
#                          with its turning mesh turret_<n>_turn and its muzzles (hp_w) under it; the ring stays in the ship mesh
#   <CODE>_base.jpg, <CODE>_orm.png, <CODE>_normal.png          the hull atlas (albedo sRGB; R occlusion, G roughness, B metal; normal)
#   <CODE>_parts_base.jpg, <CODE>_parts_orm.png, <CODE>_parts_normal.png  the sheet parts atlas
#   <CODE>_export.json     what was written: every hard point, the weapon slots, triangles, every file with its size and sha256
# Hard points (frame: +X bow, +Y up, -Z port, as every game ship):
#   hp_w<slot>_<weapon>_<arc>_<n>   one per weapon muzzle of every socket that has a "slot" in the ship json (the barrel tips and
#                                   launch mouths the kit registered while building): node -Z along the barrel, +Y away from the hull
#   hp_eng_<n>                      one per engine exit: -Z out of the bell (aft), extras.radius the bell radius
#   hp_bay_<n>                      one per hangar mouth the hull module registers (register_bay): -Z the launch direction
#   hp_breach_<n>                   breach anchors on open hull, clear of parts, counted by class and faction from one table
#                                   (tools/blender/kits/shared/hardpoints.py; docs/ship_pipeline/HARDPOINTS.md): +Y the outward
#                                   surface normal, spread over prow, mid and eng
#   hp_core                         the hull's centre of mass
#   hp_rcs_<n>                      braking puff origins: two, one port and one starboard on the forward half, -Z the braking thrust
#   hp_board_<n>                    boarding origins: two, one port and one starboard on the mid hull, -Z out toward the target
# The weapon kind and arc of each slot are read from the game's own data.js (the ship json names the ship: "game_ship"), so the
# names can never drift from the rules. tools/recipe/check_export.py then reads the written glb back and fails the export when a
# required point is missing (including the breach count for the hull's class and faction) or a hard point is off the mesh.
# The export also writes manifest_entry.json for this ship: the point counts, class, band and files, ready to merge into
# godot/assets/ships/manifest.json.
# usage: blender -b CELL.blend -P export7.py -- SHIP_JSON OUT_DIR [maps=2048] [unbaked=1]
#   unbaked=1 is for testing the geometry and hard points on a build that has not been baked (no maps are written and the
#   export json says so; check_export.py fails such a folder unless it is told the same).
import os, sys, json, math, struct, hashlib, shutil, time, random

def status(text):      # the stage file reads this (a Blender exit code is not something to lean on)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- turrets (issue 560)
# RULEBOOK 6.17 (R219): turret guns turn to face their target. A turret leaves the export as its own node turret_<n> (pivot at the
# ring centre, +Y the turning axis, -Z the rest aim), its turning mesh turret_<n>_turn and its muzzles (hp_w) as its children;
# docs/ship_pipeline/HARDPOINTS.md "Turrets". The blend marks a turret with an empty <id>_turret (turret=1) whose children are the
# turning meshes (tools/blender/kits/shared/turrets.py); a kit that names its turning pieces instead (TURRET_TURN in its kit.py)
# is marked here, in memory, before anything is read. Casemates and broadside guns are never turrets: they stay in the ship mesh.
import ast
import turrets as TURRETS

def kit_turret_turn(path):
    """the TURRET_TURN tuple a faction kit declares (read, not imported: the kit imports the build library at its top)"""
    if not os.path.exists(path): return None
    for node in ast.parse(open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()).body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(getattr(t, 'id', '') == 'TURRET_TURN' for t in node.targets):
            return tuple(ast.literal_eval(node.value))
    return None

KIT_TURN = kit_turret_turn(os.path.join(REPO, 'tools', 'blender', 'kits', str(ship.get('faction', '')), 'kit.py'))

# Wait while Ryan is playing: the game is Voidsworn.exe or a windowed Godot started with no job arguments
# (play_godot.bat passes none; every job passes --headless, --script, --bot or similar). Waiting is not timed.
function Test-RyanPlaying {
  try { $ps = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name LIKE 'Voidsworn%.exe' OR Name LIKE 'Godot%.exe'" } catch { return $false }
  foreach ($q in $ps) {
    if ($q.Name -like '*_console.exe') { continue }
    $cl = [string]$q.CommandLine
    $rest = [regex]::Replace($cl, '^\s*("[^"]*"|\S+)', '')
    $rest = [regex]::Replace($rest, '--path\s+("[^"]*"|\S+)', '')
    if ($rest -notmatch '--?\w') { return $true }
  }
  return $false
}

function Update-Line("'$file,$before,$after) {
  $path=(Resolve-Path $file).Path
  $original=[IO.File]::ReadAllText($path)
  $sep=if($original.Contains("`r`n")){"`r`n"}else{"`n"}
  $after=$after.Replace("`r`n","`n").Replace("`n",$sep)
  if(!$original.Contains($before)){throw "Missing copy line in $file"}
  [IO.File]::WriteAllText($path,$original.Replace($before,$after))
}

// Benchmarks take solo themselves, including direct tmo launches. Follow scene
// and script resources, so a scene's script cannot hide timing behind a .tscn.
function modeFor(exe, args, cwd = process.cwd(), requested = '') {
  const godot = /^(?:Godot|Voidsworn).*\.exe$/i.test(path.win32.basename(exe)) || /^godot(?:[34])?$/i.test(path.basename(exe));
  const blender = /^blender(?:\.exe)?$/i.test(path.win32.basename(exe));
  if (!godot && !blender) return requested === 'solo' || requested === 'shared' ? requested : '';
  if (godot && /(?:^|\s)--headless(?:\s|$)/i.test(args)) return '';
  if (requested === 'solo') return 'solo';
  // Only explicitly marked CPU-only Blender steps can skip a Blender claim.
  // Godot still detects GPU work and takes solo for timing scripts.
  if (blender) return requested === 'none' ? '' : 'shared';
  // Known benches remain solo even if their checkout has not been prepared yet.
  if (/--(?:bench|benchmark|measure)\b|bench209|scene_gate|bench\d|frame[_-]?time|performance|perf_probe/i.test(args) && !/--still\b/.test(args)) return 'solo';
  const project = /--path\s+(?:"([^"]+)"|(\S+))/.exec(args);
  const base = project ? path.resolve(cwd, project[1] || project[2]) : cwd;
  const visited = new Set();
  function measures(resource) {
    if (visited.has(resource)) return false;
    visited.add(resource);
    if (visited.size > 256) throw new Error('GPU resource scan too large; use PC_GPU_MODE=solo');
    let source;
    try { source = fs.readFileSync(resource.startsWith('res://') ? path.join(base, resource.slice(6)) : path.resolve(cwd, resource), 'utf8'); }
    catch (e) { if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return false; throw e; }
    source = source.replace(/^\s*#.*$/gm, '');
    if (/TIME_(?:PROCESS|FPS)|get_frame_setup_time_cpu|get_ticks_usec|frame[_ ]?(?:ms|times?)|gpu_ms|percentile|median/i.test(source)) return true;
    // Follow scene attachments, not every production preload in a capture script.
    // Effects use microsecond clocks for animation even when no speed is measured.
    return resource.endsWith('.tscn') && [...source.matchAll(/res:\/\/[^"'\s)]+\.(?:gd|tscn)/g)].some(m => measures(m[0]));
  }
  const resources = [...args.matchAll(/res:\/\/[^"'\s]+\.(?:gd|tscn)/g)].map(m => m[0]);
  const script = /--script\s+(?:"([^"]+)"|(\S+))/.exec(args);
  if (script) resources.push(script[1] || script[2]);
  if (!resources.length) {
    try {
      const config = fs.readFileSync(path.join(base, 'project.godot'), 'utf8');
      const main = /^run\/main_scene="(res:\/\/[^"\r\n]+)"/m.exec(config);
      if (main) resources.push(main[1]);
    } catch (e) { if (e.code !== 'ENOENT') throw e; }
  }
  return resources.some(measures) ? 'solo' : 'shared';
}

// Lanes C (board_c) and D (board_d) are code only (R268, R301). The runner flag or the working folder is enough (issue 947).
  Write-Output "GPU: acquired $gpuMode claim $gpuToken"
}

func _ready() -> void:
	var a := OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
	var i := 0
	while i < a.size():
		match a[i]:
			"--out": out = a[i + 1]; i += 1
			"--facs": facs = Array(a[i + 1].split(",")); i += 1
			"--sets": sets = Array(a[i + 1].split(",")); i += 1
			"--codes": codes_only = Array(a[i + 1].split(",")); i += 1
			"--tag": tag = a[i + 1]; i += 1
		i += 1
	if facs.is_empty():
		facs = ORDER.duplicate()
	if out == "":
		out = OS.get_user_data_dir().path_join("a4_shots")
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(out)
	if DisplayServer.get_name() != "headless":
		# the project starts maximised: hold an exact 1920x1080 window so every shot is one size (as main.gd --window)
		for k in 4:
			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED)
			DisplayServer.window_set_size(Vector2i(1920, 1080))
			await get_tree().process_frame
	print("[a4shots] window ", DisplayServer.window_get_size(), " viewport ", get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size)
	_world()
	print("[a4shots] out ", out, " facs ", facs, " sets ", sets)
	await _run()
	print("[a4shots] done")
	ShipView.clear_static()
	PG.finish(0)


# the battle's world (battle.gd _build_world and _apply_quality "max", then G4's look.apply), without the board
func _world() -> void:
	env = Environment.new()
	var man := ShipView.manifest()
	var sky_res := str(man.get("sky", ""))
	if sky_res != "" and ResourceLoader.exists(sky_res):
		var sh := Shader.new()
		sh.code = "shader_type sky;\nuniform sampler2D pano : source_color, filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic, repeat_enable;\nvoid sky() {\n\tvec3 c = texture(pano, SKY_COORDS).rgb;\n\tCOLOR = min(c * 0.8, vec3(0.6));\n}\n"
		var pano := ShaderMaterial.new()
		pano.shader = sh
		pano.set_shader_parameter("pano", load(sky_res))
		var sky := Sky.new()
		sky.sky_material = pano
		sky.radiance_size = Sky.RADIANCE_SIZE_256
		env.background_mode = Environment.BG_SKY
		env.sky = sky
		env.reflected_light_source = Environment.REFLECTION_SOURCE_SKY
	else:
		env.background_mode = Environment.BG_COLOR
		env.background_color = Color(0.01, 0.012, 0.02)
	env.ambient_light_source = Environment.AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR
	env.ambient_light_color = Color(1, 1, 1)
	env.ambient_light_energy = 0.5
	env.tonemap_mode = Environment.TONE_MAPPER_ACES
	env.tonemap_white = 8.0
	env.glow_enabled = true
	var we := WorldEnvironment.new()
	we.environment = env
	add_child(we)
	var key := DirectionalLight3D.new()
	key.transform = Transform3D(Basis.looking_at(KEY_DIR.normalized(), Vector3.UP), Vector3.ZERO)
	key.light_color = KEY_COL
	key.light_energy = 2.0
	key.shadow_enabled = true
	key.directional_shadow_mode = DirectionalLight3D.SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS
	key.directional_shadow_max_distance = 600.0
	add_child(key)
	var fill := DirectionalLight3D.new()
	fill.transform = Transform3D(Basis.looking_at(FILL_DIR.normalized(), Vector3.UP), Vector3.ZERO)
	fill.light_color = FILL_COL
	fill.light_energy = 0.5
	add_child(fill)
	var vp := get_viewport()
	vp.msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_4X
	RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas_set_size(4096, true)
	if ResourceLoader.exists("res://render/look.gd"):
		load("res://render/look.gd").apply(env, key, fill, {"quality": "max"})
		key.directional_shadow_max_distance = 600.0
	rig = CamRig.new()
	rig.input_enabled = false
	add_child(rig)
	cam = Camera3D.new()
	cam.fov = 30.0
	cam.near = 0.2
	cam.far = 5000.0
	add_child(cam)


func _ships_of(fac: String) -> Array:
	var r: Array = []
	for k in HT.AI_HULLS:
		var p: PackedStringArray = k.split("|")
		if p[0] == fac:
			var code: String = HT.AI_HULLS[k]
			if codes_only.is_empty() or codes_only.has(code):
				r.append([code, p[1]])
	return r


func _len_of(fac: String, cls: String) -> float:
	if fac == "obj":
		return 46.0
	if fac == "craft":
		return HT.CLS_LEN["Squadron"] * HT.SHIP_K * 4.0
	return HT.CLS_LEN.get(cls, 10.0) * HT.SHIP_K


func _spawn(code: String, fac: String, cls: String, pos: Vector3, facing := 0) -> Node3D:
	var f2 := fac if HT.FAC3D.has(fac) else "hegemony"
	var L := _len_of(fac, cls)
	var sv = ShipView.new()
	add_child(sv)
	sv.setup({"id": code, "fac": f2, "cls": cls, "facing": facing, "code": code, "L": L}, pos, true)
	sv.set_process(false)
	if "fx_engines" in sv:
		sv.fx_engines = true
	for e in sv.engines:
		(e as Node3D).visible = false
	return sv


func _run() -> void:
	if sets.has("props"):
		await _props(false)
		await _props(true)
	for f in facs:
		var ships := _ships_of(f)
		if ships.is_empty():
			continue
		if sets.has("diag"):
			for e in ships:
				var sv := _spawn(e[0], f, e[1], Vector3.ZERO)
				_diag(sv, e[0])
				sv.free()

import functools
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

from PIL import Image
from io_scene_gltf2.blender.exp.material import encode_image

times = defaultdict(float)
calls = defaultdict(int)

def measure(function, key):
    @functools.wraps(function)
    def measured(*args, **kwargs):
        label = key(*args, **kwargs)
        start = perf_counter()
        try:
            return function(*args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            times[label] += perf_counter() - start
            calls[label] += 1
    return measured

encode_image._encode_temp_image = measure(encode_image._encode_temp_image,
                                           lambda image, fmt, settings: 'Blender encode ' + fmt)
Image.Image.save = measure(Image.Image.save, lambda image, fp, format=None, **kwargs: 'Pillow save ' + str(format))

scope = dict(__file__=str(path), __name__='__main__',
             measure_resize=lambda fn: measure(fn, lambda image, role: 'resize ' + role))
start = perf_counter()
try:
    exec(compile(source, str(path), 'exec'), scope)
finally:
    for label, seconds in sorted(times.items()):
        print(f'PROFILE {label} {calls[label]} {seconds:.3f} s', flush=True)
    print(f'PROFILE total {perf_counter() - start:.3f} s', flush=True)

#!/bin/sh
# Runs the headless Godot checks named in godot/tools/ci/godot_checks.txt (issue 359 part b). GitHub runs it; so can any
# Linux checkout with Godot 4.7.2:   GODOT=/path/to/godot sh godot/tools/ci/run_checks.sh [name ...]
# First it proves the list is whole: every .gd file under godot/**/test/ is listed once, and every listed file exists.
# Then each headless line (except the ones another named step runs) runs with a time limit. A check fails on a non-zero
# exit, on the time limit, or on any SCRIPT ERROR line in its log. Prints one line per check and exits 1 on any failure.
# The whole list also has a time budget (GODOT_CHECKS_BUDGET, 780 s; a healthy run takes about 200 s): a check gets
# 300 s or what is left of the budget, whichever is less, and a check the budget never reached is a FAIL, never a quiet
# skip. So this script always ends well inside GitHub's 30 minute job limit, and a red job stays red instead of being
# cancelled (a script that does not compile makes several checks sit until their limit: commit 138ff38, 1020 s).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." || exit 1
P=$(pwd)            # godot/
ROOT=$(cd .. && pwd)
G="${GODOT:-godot}"
LIST="$P/tools/ci/godot_checks.txt"
T="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/godot_checks"
rm -rf "$T"; mkdir -p "$T/logs" "$T/fixtures" "$T/xdg"
F=0
BUDGET="${GODOT_CHECKS_BUDGET:-780}"

# 1. the list is whole
grep -v '^#' "$LIST" | grep -v '^$' | cut -d'|' -f2 | sort > "$T/listed.txt"
find . \( -path ./.godot -o -path ./gen \) -prune -o -path '*/test/*' -name '*.gd' -print | sed 's|^\./||' | sort > "$T/found.txt"
dup=$(uniq -d "$T/listed.txt")
miss=$(comm -13 "$T/listed.txt" "$T/found.txt")
gone=$(comm -23 "$T/listed.txt" "$T/found.txt")
bad=$(grep -v '^#' "$LIST" | grep -v '^$' | awk -F'|' 'NF != 5 || ($1 != "headless" && $1 != "gpu" && $1 != "retired") {print}')
if [ -n "$dup$miss$gone$bad" ]; then
  [ -n "$miss" ] && echo "  list: FAIL, test scripts not in godot_checks.txt:" && echo "$miss" | sed 's/^/    /'
  [ -n "$gone" ] && echo "  list: FAIL, listed but missing:" && echo "$gone" | sed 's/^/    /'
  [ -n "$dup" ] && echo "  list: FAIL, listed twice:" && echo "$dup" | sed 's/^/    /'
  [ -n "$bad" ] && echo "  list: FAIL, lines that are not class|script|setup|args|reason:" && echo "$bad" | sed 's/^/    /'
  F=$((F+1))
else
  echo "  list: PASS ($(wc -l < "$T/found.txt") test scripts: $(grep -c '^headless|' "$LIST") headless, $(grep -c '^gpu|' "$LIST") gpu, $(grep -c '^retired|' "$LIST") retired)"
fi

# 2. the headless checks
ran=0; t_all=$(date +%s)
grep '^headless|' "$LIST" > "$T/headless.txt"
while IFS='|' read -r cls script setup args reason; do
  name=$(basename "$script" .gd)
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then case " $* " in *" $name "*) ;; *) continue ;; esac; fi
  case "$setup" in step:*) echo "  $name: in its own step (${setup#step:})"; continue ;; esac
  left=$(( BUDGET - ( $(date +%s) - t_all ) ))
  if [ $left -le 0 ]; then echo "  $name: FAIL (not run: the list's $BUDGET s budget was used up by the checks above)"; F=$((F+1)); continue; fi
  lim=300; [ $left -lt $lim ] && lim=$left
  xdg="$T/xdg"
  a=""
  case "$setup" in
    fixture:*)
      fx="$T/fixtures/$name.json"
      if ! node "$ROOT/contrib/opus/tools/${setup#fixture:}" "$fx" > "$T/logs/$name.fixture.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null; then
        echo "  $name: FAIL (fixtures: node contrib/opus/tools/${setup#fixture:})"; tail -5 "$T/logs/$name.fixture.log" | sed 's/^/    /'; F=$((F+1)); continue
      fi ;;
    userdir) xdg="$ROOT/.onboarding_checks/xdg"; mkdir -p "$xdg" ;;
    -) ;;
    *) echo "  $name: FAIL (unknown setup $setup)"; F=$((F+1)); continue ;;
  esac
  [ "$args" != "-" ] && a=$(printf '%s' "$args" | sed "s|{fixture}|$T/fixtures/$name.json|g; s|{repo}|$ROOT|g")
  t0=$(date +%s)
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  XDG_DATA_HOME="$xdg" timeout -k 10 $lim "$G" --headless --path "$P" --script "res://$script" ${a:+--} $a > "$T/logs/$name.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null
  code=$?
  se=$(grep -c 'SCRIPT ERROR' "$T/logs/$name.log")
  s=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 )); ran=$((ran+1))
  if [ $code -eq 0 ] && [ "$se" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "  $name: PASS (${s} s)"
  else
    why="exit code $code"; [ $code -eq 124 ] && why="time limit ($lim s)"; [ $code -eq 137 ] && why="time limit ($lim s), had to be killed"; [ "$se" -gt 0 ] && why="$why, $se SCRIPT ERROR line(s)"
    echo "  $name: FAIL ($why)"
    grep -E 'SCRIPT ERROR|FAIL|ERROR' "$T/logs/$name.log" | grep -v 'leaked\|still in use' | head -8 | sed 's/^/    /'

def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(repo), *args], stderr=subprocess.PIPE)


@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def revision(repo):
    commit = git(repo, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').decode().strip()
    if not re.fullmatch(r'[a-f0-9]{40,64}', commit):
        raise ValueError('picture source has no full git commit')
    changes = git(repo, 'diff', '--binary', 'HEAD')
    # Include new source files as well as tracked edits. Do not hash PC assets.
    for name in git(repo, 'ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard', '-z').decode().split('\0'):
        if name and name != 'CODEX_TASK.md' and Path(name).suffix in {'.py', '.gd', '.js', '.ps1', '.bat'}:
            changes += name.encode() + b'\0' + (Path(repo) / name).read_bytes()
    return dict(source_commit=commit, source_dirty=bool(changes),
                source_diff_sha256=digest(changes) if changes else '')


def text_lines(record):
    lines = [record['picture_name']]
    for src in record['sources']:
        rev = src['source_commit'][:12]
        if 'source_commit_date' in src:
            rev = 'built from ' + rev
        elif src['source_dirty']:
            rev += ' + working ' + src['source_diff_sha256'][:8]
        line = rev + ' | ' + src['stage']
        if line not in lines:
            lines.append(line)
    lines.append(record['stage'] + ' | ' + record['date'])
    return lines


def strip_for(record, size):
    # One bitmap alphabet for Python and Godot, independent of installed fonts.
    glyphs = json.loads((Path(__file__).with_name('picture_font.json')).read_text())
    scale = 2 if size[0] >= 1000 else 1
    width = size[0] // scale
    lines = []
    for text in text_lines(record):
        while text:
            end = max(1, (width - 12) // 6)
            lines.append(text[:end])
            text = text[end:]
    height = len(lines) * 13 + 10
    if height * scale > size[1]:
        raise ValueError('picture is too small for a readable provenance strip')
    strip_width = min(width, max(len(t) * 6 for t in lines) + 12)
    strip = Image.new('RGB', (strip_width, height), '#10151e')
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(strip)
    draw.line((0, 0, strip_width, 0), fill='#e8b56b')
    for row, text in enumerate(lines):
        for col, char in enumerate(text):
            for y, bits in enumerate(glyphs.get(char, glyphs['?'])):
                for x in range(6):
                    if bits & (1 << (5 - x)):
                        draw.point((6 + col * 6 + x, 4 + row * 13 + y), fill='#f1e8d9')
    return strip.resize((strip.width * scale, height * scale), Image.Resampling.NEAREST)


def summary(record):
    keys = ('picture_name', 'source_commit', 'source_dirty', 'source_diff_sha256',
            'stage', 'date', 'image_sha256', 'sources')
    result = {k: record[k] for k in keys}
    if 'source_commit_date' in record:
        result['source_commit_date'] = record['source_commit_date']
    return result


def verify(path):
    path = Path(path)
    record = json.loads(sidecar(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    if record.get('schema') != 1 or record.get('picture_name') != path.name:
        raise ValueError('wrong picture name or provenance schema: ' + str(path))
    if record.get('stage') not in STAGES:
        raise ValueError('missing or invalid picture stage: ' + str(path))
    datetime.strptime(record['date'], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
    for src in [record] + record['sources']:
        if not re.fullmatch(r'[a-f0-9]{40,64}', src['source_commit']) or src['stage'] not in STAGES:
            raise ValueError('invalid source revision/stage: ' + str(path))
        if src['source_dirty'] and not re.fullmatch(r'[a-f0-9]{64}', src['source_diff_sha256']):
            raise ValueError('working revision lacks its digest: ' + str(path))
        if 'source_commit_date' in src:
            datetime.strptime(src['source_commit_date'], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
            if src['source_dirty'] or src['source_diff_sha256']:
                raise ValueError('build revision has a working-tree state: ' + str(path))
    if not record['sources'] or record['image_sha256'] != digest(path.read_bytes()):
        raise ValueError('picture changed after stamping: ' + str(path))
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        box = record['stamp_box']
        frames = [f.copy() for f in ImageSequence.Iterator(image)]
        if len(frames) != len(record['strip_sha256']):
            raise ValueError('picture frame count changed: ' + str(path))
        for frame, expected in zip(frames, record['strip_sha256']):
            strip = frame.convert('RGB').crop(box)
            if digest(strip.tobytes()) != expected or strip.size != tuple(record['strip_size']):
                raise ValueError('missing burned-in strip: ' + str(path))
            template = strip_for(record, image.size)
            if template.size != strip.size or digest(template.tobytes()) != record['stamp_template_sha256']:
                raise ValueError('invalid stamp bounds: ' + str(path))
            # JPEG and GIF quantize pixels. The text still has to be present.
            from PIL import ImageChops, ImageStat
            if max(ImageStat.Stat(ImageChops.difference(strip, template)).mean) > 18:
                raise ValueError('provenance text is absent from the picture: ' + str(path))
    return record


def open_picture(path, required=False):
    """Restore only the pixels hidden by the strip, for crops and measurements."""
    path = Path(path)
    record = verify(path) if sidecar(path).exists() or required else None
    with Image.open(path) as original:
        image = original.copy()
    if record:
        patch = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(record['covered_pixels'][0])))
        image = image.convert(patch.mode)
        image.paste(patch, tuple(record['stamp_box'][:2]))
    return image


def save_picture(image, path, stage, sources=None, repo=None, **options):
    if stage not in STAGES:
        raise ValueError('unknown picture stage: ' + stage)
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() not in EXTENSIONS:
        raise ValueError('unsupported review image: ' + str(path))
    source_list = []
    for record in sources or []:
        for src in record['sources']:
            if src not in source_list:
                source_list.append(src)
    if not source_list:
        source_list = [dict(revision(str(Path(repo or ROOT).resolve())), stage=stage)]
    record = dict(source_list[0], schema=1, picture_name=path.name, stage=stage,
                  date=datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'),
                  sources=source_list, inputs=[summary(s) for s in sources or []])
    strip = strip_for(record, image.size)
    box = [0, image.height - strip.height, strip.width, image.height]
    frames = [image] + list(options.pop('append_images', []))
    covered = []
    stamped = []
    for frame in frames:
        frame = frame.copy().convert('RGBA' if 'A' in frame.getbands() and path.suffix.lower() not in {'.jpg', '.jpeg'} else 'RGB')
        if frame.size != image.size:
            raise ValueError('animation frames must have the same size')
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        frame.crop(box).save(buf, format='PNG')
        covered.append(base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode('ascii'))
        frame.paste(strip, tuple(box[:2]))
        stamped.append(frame)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if len(stamped) > 1:
        options.update(save_all=True, append_images=stamped[1:])
    stamped[0].save(path, **options)
    with Image.open(path) as saved:
        strips = [digest(f.convert('RGB').crop(box).tobytes()) for f in ImageSequence.Iterator(saved)]
    record.update(stamp_box=box, strip_size=list(strip.size), strip_sha256=strips,
                  stamp_template_sha256=digest(strip.tobytes()),
                  covered_pixels=covered, image_sha256=digest(path.read_bytes()))
    sidecar(path).write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
    return record


def stamp_file(path, stage, repo=None, new_render=False):
    path = Path(path)
    if sidecar(path).exists() and not new_render:
        # Never turn a cached old capture into a new revision.
        return verify(path)
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        frames = [f.convert('RGBA') for f in ImageSequence.Iterator(image)]
        options = {}
        if image.format == 'GIF':
            options.update(duration=image.info.get('duration', 100), loop=image.info.get('loop', 0))
        elif image.format == 'JPEG':
            options.update(quality=95)
    return save_picture(frames[0], path, stage, repo=repo, append_images=frames[1:], **options)


class Review:
    """Collect inputs for one output at a time.

    take_sources reserves inputs alongside cached pixels. Pass those records to
    save(sources=...) whenever another output uses the same cached pictures.
    """
    def __init__(self, stage):
        self.stage = stage
        self.sources = []

    def open(self, path, reference=False):
        if not reference or sidecar(path).exists():
            record = verify(path)
            if record not in self.sources:
                self.sources.append(record)
        return open_picture(path)

    def take_sources(self):
        sources, self.sources = self.sources, []
        return sources

    def save(self, image, path, sources=(), **options):
        output_sources = []
        for source in [*sources, *self.sources]:
            if source not in output_sources:
                output_sources.append(source)
        if not output_sources:
            raise ValueError('review sheet needs stamped source pictures; rerun the capture, do not relabel an old picture')
        record = save_picture(image, path, self.stage, sources=output_sources, **options)
        self.sources.clear()
        return record
